title.narrative: Promoting trade and investment in Angola

description.narrative: Since 2018, the Government of Angola has implemented reforms, including legislative and regulatory updates to promote public institutions dynamism, increase private sector competition, and to attract Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in non-oil sectors. Firstly, the Private Investment and Export Promotion Agency of Angola (AIPEX) was established under Presidential Decree 81/18 of 19 March 2018, resulting from the merger of the former Technical Unit for Private Investment - U.T.I.P and the Agency for the Promotion of Investment and Exports of Angola (AIPEX) aiming to increase investment attraction and exports promotion. Secondly, the Private Investment Law (Lei nº. 10/18) was sanctioned to establish and update benefits and stimulate private investment in non-oil sectors. However, the promotion of investment, trade and exports still presents glaring weaknesses for the achievement of the objectives that are advocated in the National Development Plan 2023-2027 of the Republic of Angola (2023-2027) and in the Production Support, Export Diversification, and Import Substitution Program (PRODESI 2.0). Investment, trade, and exports are constrained by restrictions in public institutional procedures, deriving from weak technical capacities, lack of inter-service coordination and inexistent interoperability of digital platforms, crucial to improve the efficiency and transparency needed to increase in FDI and trade.Visualising a window of opportunity based on the fruitful relationship of the European Union (EU) with the Angolan government, the Angola-EU dialogue mechanism identified three priority areas, aligned with the National Development Plan 2023-2027 of the Republic of Angola, as well as the Team Europe Initiative: (i) Sustainable economic diversification, including agriculture and agro-logistics; (ii) Good governance and social inclusion with emphasis on rule of law, institutional strengthening, digital and economic governance, and (iii) Human development, focusing on technical vocational education and training, among other aspects.The Action aims to promote and increase a more sustainable investment, trade, and exports business environment. The specific objectives of the Action are: (1) Improve Angola¿s attractiveness to investments; (2) Facilitate trade and exports; (3) Support interoperability of digital platforms. All these specific objectives will be instigated through technical assistance and capacity building of the identified stakeholders.The Action aligns with Angola's Long Term Development Strategy and with the specific needs indicated by the national stakeholders involved in its formulation which include the national institutions responsible for trade, investment and export promotion that operate in public sector, private sector, and civil society. The Action will contribute to Priority area 1 (Sustainable economic diversification), Specific objective 1 (Improved competitiveness and sustainability of the local private sector in Angola), of the 2021-2027 MIP for Angola.
